$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Container registries. See aws/s3.json for the contract. 'nano' = Nano/dev_server (core/azure_arm_core.py + core/azure_acr_core.py + core/azure_locks_core.py); 'offline' = the appliance, which shares the same generic ARM catalog.

azure.acr.registry.crud.title: Registries — create, get, list, delete (generic ARM catalog)

azure.acr.registry.listactions.title: "Manage view", "Open query" (Azure Resource Graph) and "Assign tags" on the registries list
limitations: "Manage view" is the lens kit's own column chooser (BrowseGrid), a console preference that needs no backend. "Open query" runs a real, minimal KQL subset (table Resources/ResourceContainers, where/project/limit/order by/count) evaluated over the ARM engine's own resource store — not a canned response, but not full Kusto either (no joins, summarize, or time-series operators). "Assign tags" PATCHes real ARM tags onto every selected registry.

azure.acr.admin_credentials.title: Admin user credentials (listCredentials / regenerateCredential)
limitations: The admin username/passwords are generated and rotated for real and persist on the registry, but Vyomi's repository data plane never checks them (or any other credential) — a docker/oras client can push and pull without presenting them.

azure.acr.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this registry
limitations: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM at resource, resource-group and subscription scope (CanNotDelete/ReadOnly, name and notes validated); this blade manages the locks scoped to this container registry only and has no scope switch. A resource-group or subscription lock really blocks writes and deletes of everything under it with 409 ScopeLocked (core/azure_arm_ext_core.py lock_conflict), but a lock set directly on a container registry is stored and listed only: it does not block writes or deletes of the container registry itself.

azure.acr.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: A simplified, generic ARM activity feed (create/update/delete on this resource), not the real Microsoft.Insights audit trail (callers, correlation ids, full operation metadata); severity/timespan filtering and the secondary toolbar (Edit columns, Export, Insights, Feedback) are not modeled.

azure.acr.repositories.title: Repositories and tags, over the OCI/Docker Registry v2 wire and the ACR REST repository-metadata extension
limitations: Repositories are process-global (not scoped to one registry's login server), the same simplification Key Vault's keys/secrets data planes make. Blob content is stored and digest-verified but never unpacked/executed — Vyomi doesn't run containers.

azure.acr.webhooks.title: Webhooks (Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/webhooks)
limitations: Webhook definitions round-trip through ARM for real (create/list/delete, scoped to this registry), but Vyomi never fires them — a push/delete/quarantine event on this registry never POSTs to the configured Service URI, and there is no Ping action.

azure.acr.iam.title: Access control (IAM): role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions). The Role assignments list is ENFORCED scoped to this registry (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view) instead of the whole subscription — the same engine the VM/NSG/Cosmos DB blades use; Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too). Assignments are still created at the subscription scope (az role assignment create), and 'Check access' / 'My access' evaluation and Deny assignments / Classic administrators remain an honest gap. Update: the Deny assignments list, Classic administrators (a read-only list of the subscription's account administrator, like the real API) and My access (the simulated signed-in principal, evaluated with checkAccess) are now real shared tabs (azure.common.*); the gap wording above predates them.

azure.acr.overview_tabs.title: Overview Monitoring, Capabilities and Recommendations tabs
limitations: Monitoring shows a live snapshot of this registry's own state (repository/webhook/geo-replication counts read off the real data plane and ARM child resources) — Vyomi doesn't meter push/pull bandwidth over time, so there is no historical throughput chart. Capabilities computes a real Yes/No feature matrix from the registry's actual sku tier, not a static reference table. Recommendations reuses the same live Defender for Cloud rule engine as the Microsoft Defender for Cloud blade (azure.acr.defender / azure.defender.recommendations).

azure.acr.monitoring.title: Insights, Alerts, Metrics, Diagnostic settings and Logs
limitations: Diagnostic settings (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings) is a real ARM extension resource scoped to this registry: logs/metrics are stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires, but never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline. Insights, Alerts, Metrics and Logs are the shared per-resource panels (azure.common.resource_monitoring): the only metric is the registry's own Activity-log operation count, there is no pull/push or storage telemetry.

azure.acr.exporttemplate_formats.title: Export template — ARM, Bicep and Terraform formats, generated client-side from this registry
limitations: Download, Add to library, Deploy and Visualize template are honest 'Not simulated' actions — only template generation (ARM/Bicep/Terraform) from the registry's current ARM properties is real.

azure.acr.create_fields.title: Domain name label scope and Role assignment permissions mode (create wizard)
limitations: Both 2025 ARM additions are stored on the registry's own properties for real (ARM PUT/GET round-trip), surfaced in Properties/Essentials and included in Export template — Vyomi does not model a DNS-label-reuse layer or an ABAC-repository-permission ENGINE for them to additionally gate (repository-scoped Tokens/Scope maps remain usable regardless of the selected mode, same as real ACR's own RBAC-vs-ABAC rollout).

azure.acr.defender.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (this container registry's recommendations)
limitations: Shows the live Defender for Cloud recommendations for this resource from Vyomi's rule engine (see azure.defender.recommendations); Azure's full built-in recommendation catalogue is not reproduced.

azure.acr.quickstart.title: Quick start
limitations: Docker/az-acr sign-in, push and pull snippets are generated from this registry's own live login server and admin-user state — there is nothing further to simulate.

azure.acr.events.title: Events
limitations: Event Grid system topics scoped to this registry (Microsoft.EventGrid/systemTopics, filtered by source) are real, stored ARM resources using the same engine the Event Grid service itself ships — but, like Webhooks, Vyomi never actually fires a push/delete event at a subscriber endpoint.

azure.acr.encryption.title: Encryption
limitations: Customer-managed key encryption is ENFORCED Premium-only (server-side, not just a disabled UI control) and requires a system assigned managed identity to be turned on first, same as real ACR requiring an identity to reach the key. The key identifier is stored and round-tripped for real; Vyomi does not re-encrypt or validate repository content against the referenced Key Vault key.

azure.acr.identity.title: Identity
limitations: System assigned managed identity mints a real, stable principalId/tenantId (generic over every ARM catalog type, core/azure_arm_core.py's _apply_identity) that persists across PUT/PATCH and clears on 'None'.

User assigned identities are real: the identity block can reference Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities resources (create them in the Managed Identities service), an unknown reference is rejected with 400 ResourceNotFound, and the attached identity's principalId/clientId are resolved from that resource. The identity is not used to authorize anything: a managed identity only matters as the subject of a role assignment on Access control (IAM).

azure.acr.networking.title: Networking
limitations: Disabling public network access is ENFORCED on the registry's own data-plane endpoint for real (push/pull/_catalog/… are rejected with a 403 while it's off — core/azure_arm_core.py's acr_network_denied, wired through the x-vyomi-registry header in core/aws_wire_router.py and core/wire_ingress.py) and is Premium-gated server-side. Vyomi has no private-endpoint/VNet path to let a caller back in, and per-IP firewall allow-list rules are not evaluated (same simplification Key Vault's own networking makes).

azure.acr.georeplications.title: Geo-replications
limitations: Replication resources are real, Premium-gated nested ARM child resources, server-side validated (no replicating to the registry's own primary location, no duplicate-region replication). Actual cross-region data redundancy isn't modeled — this registry's repositories are already a single process-global store (see azure.acr.repositories).

azure.acr.tasks.title: Tasks
limitations: Task definitions are real, Standard+-gated ARM resources; runs are REAL builds through the shared CI seam (core/azure_acr_tasks_core.py): POST registries/{r}/scheduleRun with DockerBuildRequest or TaskRunRequest builds the context (a https://github.com/{o}/{r}[#branch] URL, fetched with the user's own PAT when one is connected, or inline vyomiFiles) with BuildKit on the offline appliance (Dockerfile validated, --pull=false so only base images already on the host are used) and records a registries/runs record with the build log and outputImages only when an image was really built. Nano has no container runtime, so image runs are recorded Failed with that reason (never a fake success). The built image is exported (docker save) and PUSHED into the simulated registry's repository store under every imageName (blobs + schema2 manifest, listed by az acr repository, pullable over /v2), unless isPushEnabled is false or the image exceeds 300 MB. Limits: FileTaskRunRequest/EncodedTaskRunRequest multi-step YAML tasks are rejected; source/timer/base-image triggers do not fire automatically; Azure Repos/Bitbucket/generic git sources are not fetchable.

azure.acr.cache.title: Cache
limitations: Cache rule definitions are real, Premium-gated nested ARM child resources, server-side validated (each target repository can only be mapped by one rule). Vyomi never actually fetches from the upstream registry — nothing leaves the simulator.

azure.acr.connectedregistries.title: Connected registries
limitations: Connected registry definitions are real, Premium-gated nested ARM child resources. Vyomi runs no edge/offline sync agent, so content never actually replicates to one.

azure.acr.tokens.title: Tokens
limitations: Token resources are real, Premium-gated nested ARM child resources: a token's scopeMapId is server-side validated against a real scope map on the same registry. Tokens are not wired to the data plane's own authentication — a docker/oras client is never actually challenged for one (same gap as azure.acr.admin_credentials).

azure.acr.scopemaps.title: Scope maps
limitations: Scope map resources are real, Premium-gated nested ARM child resources: `actions` entries are server-side validated against the real grammar (<repository>:<content|metadata>/<read|write|delete>[,...]). They are not enforced against the data plane's own authorization (same gap as Tokens).

azure.acr.retention.title: Retention (Preview)
limitations: ENFORCED for real: once enabled, an untagged manifest is purged after it has gone untagged for longer than the configured number of days (core/azure_acr_core.py's purge_untagged, swept on every data-plane call via the x-vyomi-registry header) — not a stored setting nobody acts on. Because repositories are process-global (azure.acr.repositories), the policy that applies during a sweep is whichever registry's data-plane call triggered it, not cleanly isolated per registry if more than one registry has retention enabled at once.

azure.acr.import.title: Import image (copy between repositories/registries)
limitations: Copies a manifest and every blob it references to the target tags (NoForce refuses to overwrite a different digest, Force retags). Sources outside Vyomi (Docker Hub, MCR, GHCR) are refused because there is no internet egress.

Vyomi keeps one repository store shared by all its registries, so a source image is looked up by repository name across that shared store, and the action is carried on the data plane (POST /acr/v1/_import) rather than the ARM importImage action, so `az acr import` is not supported.
